nodes.label: Spinal cord
nodes.desc: A central nervous system structure that conducts information between the brain and body and supports spinal reflexes.

nodes.label: Brainstem
nodes.desc: The brainstem comprises the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.

nodes.label: Left cerebral hemisphere
nodes.desc: The left cerebral hemisphere, containing cortical and subcortical structures.

nodes.label: Right cerebral hemisphere
nodes.desc: The right cerebral hemisphere, containing cortical and subcortical structures.

nodes.label: Left insula
nodes.desc: The left insular cortex, contributing to interoception, salience processing and integration of bodily and cognitive information.

nodes.label: Left prefrontal cortex
nodes.desc: A broad left prefrontal region involved in executive control, working memory and goal-directed behavior.

nodes.label: Left primary motor cortex
nodes.desc: The left primary motor cortex, contributing to voluntary motor execution, predominantly controlling the contralateral body.

nodes.label: Left premotor cortex
nodes.desc: A lateral frontal motor region involved in movement preparation and sensorimotor transformations.

nodes.label: Left Broca area
nodes.desc: A language-related region in the left inferior frontal gyrus, with functions extending beyond speech production.

nodes.label: Left primary somatosensory cortex
nodes.desc: The left primary somatosensory cortex, processing tactile and proprioceptive information from the contralateral body.

nodes.label: Left posterior parietal cortex
nodes.desc: A region involved in multisensory integration, spatial representation and sensorimotor coordination.

nodes.label: Left primary auditory cortex
nodes.desc: The left primary auditory cortex, involved in the cortical processing of auditory information.

nodes.label: Left hippocampus
nodes.desc: A medial temporal structure essential to several forms of memory formation and spatial representation.

nodes.label: Left amygdala
nodes.desc: A medial temporal nuclear complex involved in emotional learning and the processing of biologically relevant stimuli.

nodes.label: Left primary visual cortex
nodes.desc: The left primary visual cortex, receiving visual information through thalamocortical pathways.

nodes.label: Thalamus
nodes.desc: A set of diencephalic nuclei involved in sensory and motor information routing and broader cortical-subcortical interactions.

nodes.label: Hypothalamus
nodes.desc: A diencephalic region involved in homeostasis, endocrine regulation and autonomic control.

nodes.label: Caudate nucleus
nodes.desc: A striatal nucleus participating in associative and action-selection circuits.

nodes.label: Putamen
nodes.desc: A striatal nucleus participating in sensorimotor and associative circuits.

nodes.label: Globus pallidus
nodes.desc: A basal ganglia structure involved in the regulation of thalamocortical activity.

nodes.label: Substantia nigra
nodes.desc: A midbrain structure with important roles in basal ganglia circuits and dopaminergic modulation.

nodes.label: Reticular formation
nodes.desc: A distributed brainstem network involved in arousal, autonomic regulation and motor functions.

nodes.label: Superior colliculus
nodes.desc: A midbrain structure involved in visual orienting and multisensory control of orienting responses.

nodes.label: Inferior colliculus
nodes.desc: A midbrain auditory structure participating in ascending auditory pathways.

nodes.label: Cerebellar cortex
nodes.desc: The layered cortical tissue of the cerebellum, involved in processing information within cerebellar circuits.

nodes.label: Dentate nucleus
nodes.desc: A deep cerebellar nucleus contributing to cerebellar output pathways.

nodes.label: Retina
nodes.desc: The light-sensitive neural tissue of the eye. Included as a sensory boundary, not as part of the brain.

nodes.label: Lateral geniculate nucleus
nodes.desc: A thalamic relay nucleus in the principal geniculostriate visual pathway.

nodes.label: Cochlea
nodes.desc: The auditory sensory organ of the inner ear. Included as a sensory boundary, not as part of the brain.

nodes.label: Medial geniculate nucleus
nodes.desc: A thalamic relay complex participating in auditory pathways to the cortex.

nodes.label: Dorsal root ganglion
nodes.desc: A peripheral sensory ganglion containing cell bodies of many primary somatosensory neurons.

nodes.label: Ventral posterior nucleus
nodes.desc: A thalamic nuclear complex relaying somatosensory information to cortical areas.

nodes.label: Entorhinal cortex
nodes.desc: A medial temporal cortical region serving as a major interface between the hippocampal formation and neocortex.

nodes.label: Subiculum
nodes.desc: A hippocampal formation subregion involved in hippocampal output pathways.

nodes.label: Fornix
nodes.desc: A major white matter pathway connecting the hippocampal formation with subcortical targets.

pathways.description: A simplified representation of the principal retinal-thalamic-cortical visual pathway.
A simplified representation of retinal projections to the superior colliculus and related orienting networks.
A simplified auditory route from the cochlea through midbrain and thalamic relay structures to auditory cortex.
A highly simplified representation of ascending somatosensory information and cortical processing.
A simplified descending motor pathway from cortical motor regions to the spinal cord.
A simplified representation of hippocampal formation output through subicular and fornical structures.
Object and face recognition (ventral visual stream, the "what" pathway).
Motion and spatial processing (dorsal visual stream, the "where" pathway).
From the cochlea to speech comprehension.
Fine touch and proprioception.
Where the pain is and how intense it is.
The emotional and unpleasant experience of pain.
The sensory pathway that initially bypasses the thalamus.
Taste processing.
Light signals regulate circadian sleep–wake rhythms.
Stabilization of gaze during head movements.
A reflex response mediated by spinal circuits without requiring cortical involvement (survival-related behavior).
Automatic regulation of breathing.
From motor intention to muscle contraction.
Transformation of sensory information into motor commands.
From comprehension to formulation and spoken expression.
From sound perception to meaning and response formulation.
Generation of rapid eye movements to shift gaze.
Disinhibition of the selected action (the "Go" pathway).
Suppression of competing actions (the "NoGo" pathway).
Rapid inhibition of an ongoing or planned action (the "Stop" pathway).
Movement correction and fine-tuning.
A classical neural circuit associated with episodic memory.
Integration of experience into long-term cortical memory.
Maintaining and manipulating information in the mind.
Rapid defensive responses before conscious awareness, such as freezing or fleeing.
Hormonal response to perceived threats.
Prefrontal regulation of amygdala activity.
Evaluation of positive and negative value and its contribution to motivation.
Dopamine signaling involved in motivation and reinforcement.
Dopamine signaling involved in attention and planning.
Dopamine signaling involved in motor control and movement initiation.
Regulation of wakefulness and attention.
